title: Best FP&A Software for Mid-Market Companies Replacing Legacy Planning Tools (Q4 2026): 8 Platforms Compared
summary: Compare 8 FP&A platforms for mid-market teams replacing legacy planning tools, with selection criteria, demo questions and migration notes.
body_markdown:
*Last updated November 18, 2026*


The best FP&A software for a mid-market company replacing a legacy planning tool is the platform your finance team can run itself, connect to your ERP, CRM and HRIS, and put into production in weeks rather than quarters. Abacum leads this comparison for upper mid-market and scaling teams, followed by Anaplan, Pigment, Planful, Workday Adaptive Planning, Vena, Cube and Datarails.


## Key takeaways


-


Mid-market teams replacing a legacy tool should shortlist on five criteria: finance-owned modeling, time to value, spreadsheet connectivity, governed AI, and a rollout plan with named owners.


-


Eight platforms are worth evaluating in Q4 2026: Abacum, Anaplan, Pigment, Planful, Workday Adaptive Planning, Vena, Cube and Datarails.


-


Ask every vendor to build one of your real planning scenarios live, and confirm who owns the model after go-live.


-


Weigh the admin and consulting support each platform needs after launch, because that cost shows up long after the contract is signed.


A legacy planning tool usually shows its age in three places. Every change request becomes a ticket, every version is reconciled by hand, and the answer to a board question arrives after the decision has been made. This guide compares eight FP&A platforms on what each one does for a mid-market finance team, and it gives you the questions to take into every demo.


## What mid-market teams should look for in FP&A software


-


**Finance-owned modeling.** Finance should be able to add a driver, a product line or a new scenario without opening a ticket.


-


**Time to value.** Leadership asks a "what if" in the morning, and the answer should be ready the same day. Ask for milestones, not just a go-live date.


-


**Spreadsheet connectivity.** Your existing models should come in, and plan work should be able to go back out to a spreadsheet.


-


**Governed AI.** Outputs should trace to source data and assumptions, and finance should approve every change to reported figures.


-


**Connected data.** Your ERP, CRM and HRIS should feed the plan without manual pulls, so actuals, headcount and pipeline reconcile.


## The 8 best FP&A platforms for mid-market companies replacing legacy tools


### 1. Abacum


Abacum is the AI-native FP&A platform finance trusts, and the business planning platform the whole company runs on. It runs on one governed layer of data, logic and context: data is the what, logic is the how, context is the why.


**Best for:** finance teams at scaling companies and the upper mid-market that are replacing spreadsheets or a legacy planning tool and want to plan weekly instead of reporting quarterly.


-


Reforecast weekly, monthly, quarterly, or whenever the business shifts, and answer the board's question the same day it is asked.


-


**AI Modeler** turns a plain-language description, or a spreadsheet you have already built, into a working model in minutes. You can add a product line or new variables by asking, even in models you inherited, and every model explains itself line by line before the board meeting. The agent proposes, our planning engine calculates, and you approve. Nothing saves until you approve.


-


**Abra** , the AI agent at the center of Abacum, takes a question in plain language, works out what it needs, and brings in the right expert agents (Modeler, Analyst, Reporter and Data Manager). It works from your governed data, models and context, every answer shows its work, and nothing changes without approval.


-


Budget owners plan in their own spaces with input templates, while finance keeps control of approvals and the final number.


-


Enterprise-grade governance and scale come built in, owned by finance and live in weeks, not quarters, with guidance from our in-house FP&A experts.


Explore our[budgeting and forecasting use case](https://www.abacum.ai/use-cases/budgeting-forecasting) , or read how we compare platforms in our guide to the[best FP&A software for replacing legacy planning](https://www.abacum.ai/blog/best-fpa-software-scaling-enterprises-replacing-legacy-planning-tools) .


### 2. Anaplan


Anaplan is a long-standing enterprise connected planning platform, known for its Hyperblock engine, extensive modeling and a large template ecosystem. **Best for:** large planning programs with dedicated model builders. **Ask:** Who builds and maintains the models after go-live?


### 3. Pigment


Pigment is a flexible modeling platform for teams that want to design and maintain their own planning models. Your team or an implementation partner designs it and keeps it running. **Best for:** teams that want to design custom models. **Ask:** Who owns the model after go-live?


### 4. Planful


Planful brings planning, reporting and close workflows together for finance teams. **Best for:** teams that want those workflows under one roof. **Ask:** How does a scenario change flow through to reports?


### 5. Workday Adaptive Planning


Workday Adaptive Planning is part of the Workday ecosystem. **Best for:** teams already running Workday for HR and financials. **Ask:** How does it connect to sources outside Workday?


### 6. Vena


Vena builds planning workflows around Microsoft Excel. **Best for:** teams standardized on Microsoft tools. **Ask:** How does the model grow as scenarios multiply?


### 7. Cube


Cube connects spreadsheets in Excel and Google Sheets to a planning layer. **Best for:** teams that want to keep working in a spreadsheet interface. **Ask:** Where do formulas and logic live as the model scales?


### 8. Datarails


Datarails automates FP&A work on top of Excel. **Best for:** teams that want Excel to stay the front end. **Ask:** What changes about version control and approvals?

## How to choose


1.


Write down the three planning scenarios leadership asks for most often.


2.


Ask each shortlisted vendor to build one live, starting from a spreadsheet you already use.


3.


Note who on your team could repeat the change next week without help.


4.


Compare rollout plans, including who owns the model after go-live.


5.


Match the platform to your situation: a Workday shop should test the Workday connection, an Excel-centered team should test how versions and approvals work, and a team that wants finance to own modeling should test how much of the setup finance can do alone.


## Migration notes: data, parallel runs and change management


Audit your historical data and decide what moves and what stays archived. Run the legacy tool and the new platform side by side through one planning cycle, and reconcile outputs before you retire the old system. Name champions on the FP&A team early, and train people on the new workflow, not just the new screens.
